# My thinking for this year

Fifty-eight years old, forty years on this same piece of ground. My son is working down in Handan now, so it's just me and my wife looking after the 7.5 mu. She has some off-farm work too — light things, helps out when I need her during the busy seasons, wheat harvest and maize planting especially. That's the squeeze: small farm, few hands.

Because I finished senior high and did the agricultural extension courses, I try to think about the numbers — expected yield, N per mu, water use — not just copy what the neighbor does. But I'm no big farm. I can't afford to waste inputs, and I can't afford a bad year either. So I plant for stability first, cash second.

**How I split the 7.5 mu.** I keep 6.5 mu in the wheat-maize rotation — that's the backbone, it feeds us and brings in the grain sale. The other 1 mu I put into spring kohlrabi. Vegetables are more work and more risk, but kohlrabi moves well in the Quzhou market in late May before everyone else's summer veg floods in. One mu of kohlrabi in a good year pays as well as three mu of wheat. That's why I keep it — it's my cash crop.

**Wheat (already in the ground).** I planted 良星99 around October 12 last fall, put down compound 15-15-15 at about 40 kg/mu as base before drilling. The wheat came through the winter fine — I walked the field last week, the tillers look good. In another ten days or so I'll do green-up irrigation and topdress urea, around 18 kg/mu at jointing. That gets me to roughly 15-16 kg N/mu total, which is about where I've settled over the last five years for this soil. After jointing I'll irrigate again, then once more at grain filling if May is dry. Three irrigations usually, maybe four if the wind comes hot. I spray herbicide in March for the wild oats and shepherd's purse. If I see stripe rust on flag leaf I'll spray once — last year I didn't, and I won't skip it again. Targeting 475 kg/mu. My five-year average is 460, conditions look normal so far.

**Maize (goes in right after wheat comes off).** The window is tight — I have maybe five days between combining the wheat and drilling the maize. I use the no-till planter from the village cooperative, costs me about 25 yuan/mu but saves two days. Seed is 郑单958, hybrid, about 4.5 kg/mu. Base fertilizer goes in with the drill — another compound, about 30 kg/mu. Then one topdress of urea at big trumpet stage, around 12-13 kg/mu. If July rains come normal I irrigate once at silking; if it's dry like 2024, I'll irrigate twice. I spray atrazine/acetochlor mix at planting, and I watch for corn borer around tasseling — if the neighbor sees them, I'll treat. Target 540 kg/mu. Our ground does better with maize than wheat.

**Kohlrabi (1 mu, spring crop).** This is the crop I take seriously because the margin is there but so is the risk. I raise seedlings in a small cold frame starting late February, transplant around March 20, harvest end of May. I use a hybrid variety I got from the seed shop in town — pays for itself in uniformity. Before transplanting I put down rotten chicken manure, about 1500 kg/mu (I get it from the layer farm north of the village for 0.3 yuan/jin), plus compound fertilizer at 50 kg/mu. That's heavy but vegetables take it. Then two side-dressings of urea during growth. Irrigate roughly every 7-10 days, five or six times total — kohlrabi can't take water stress or it cracks. Pest pressure is real: aphids and flea beetles, so I spray imidacloprid once and a pyrethroid once. My wife and I do the transplanting together over two days; at harvest I hire two day-laborers for one day, about 120 yuan each. If the market holds at 1.5-2 yuan/jin, this mu brings in 4000-5000 yuan gross.

**What I'm watching this year.** Urea price was up last fall — I paid about 2400 yuan per ton. If it doesn't ease by June I'll cut the maize topdress by a kilo or two per mu, not more. Rain in April will tell me if I need a fourth wheat irrigation. And I'm keeping an eye on the kohlrabi wholesale price in Handan in early May — if it's weak, I'll stretch my harvest into June and hope for better.
